summary: Accepted the beneficiary relationship from structural copper scarcity to Rio Tinto with medium positive sensitivity and medium confidence. Current issuer evidence shows a direct path through Oyu Tolgoi's ramp, copper volumes, costs, and cash generation, while iron-ore dominance, commodity diversification, project spending, leverage, ownership terms, and adverse current valuation limit shareholder transmission. Updated the relationship page, catalog, log, and canonical relationship row; no strategy or follow-up operation was created before the imminent half-year results.

evidence.claim: Rio Tinto reported first-half copper-equivalent production up 3%, Oyu Tolgoi first-half copper production up 31%, improved Oyu Tolgoi C1 cost guidance of USD 0.30-0.50 per pound, group second-quarter copper production of 213 kt down 7% year over year and sequentially, and unchanged 2026 copper guidance of 800-870 kt.

Rio Tinto reported 2025 operating cash flow of USD 16.832 billion, free cash flow of USD 4.025 billion down 28%, and net debt of USD 14.362 billion, showing group funding capacity but material capital-intensity and leverage counterweights to copper-specific gains.

The maintained security review records diversified mining exposure, iron-ore dominance, Oyu Tolgoi ramp potential, a USD 91.95 ADR mark, and bounded downside and base values 27.2% and 5.4% below market, blocking strategy research.

The maintained idea defines the causal channel from constrained mine supply and copper demand to low-cost producer cash flow while preserving recycling, substitution, supply response, execution, jurisdiction, capital intensity, and valuation as contrary evidence.
